decisive_items: Serum creatine phosphokinase was markedly elevated at over 90,000 U/L
response.rationale: C1 uniquely combines the AKI phenotype (oliguria, red-colored urine, low ionized calcium, elevated phosphate) with the definitive rhabdomyolysis marker (CPK >90,000). R3 captures only the renal/metabolic consequences, while R2 captures muscle symptoms but omits the decisive CPK and AKI laboratory spans; R1 rests on nonspecific infection/SIRS features.

rejected.why: Fever, cough, diarrhea, tachycardia, and hypotension are nonspecific infection/SIRS features; no confirmed source and no CPK/AKI-specific spans.
Myalgia, tenderness, and red urine are suggestive, but raw support omits the decisive CPK >90,000 and AKI electrolyte abnormalities, making it incomplete.
